claim: Let \(m\ge 2\), \(k\ge 1\), and \(\ell\ge k+1\), and let \(S_m(\ell)\) be the spider with \(m\) legs of length \(\ell\). Then the \(k\)-th graph power satisfies \[M(S_m(\ell)^k)=Z(S_m(\ell)^k)=(m-1)k.\]
integrity: The lower bound is proved by an explicit real symmetric matrix with the exact graph support and a kernel subspace of dimension (m-1)k. The upper bound is the published Proposition 9. Finite computation is used only as corroboration.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns equal-leg spiders in the regime ell >= k+1. It does not cover unequal leg lengths, the shorter-leg regime, positive-semidefinite zero forcing, or arbitrary tree powers. The motivating preprint is extremely recent, so later literature may alter the originality assessment.
title: Exact zero forcing and maximum nullity of powers of equal-leg spiders
